title: Property of the selected Noetherian compactification
statement:
The constructed $C_{Y,\lambda_Y}$ is a compactification of
$Y_{\lambda_Y}\to S_{\lambda_Y}$.

proof.text: Write $g:Y_{\lambda_Y}\to S_{\lambda_Y}$ for the selected descended morphism. By [lemma-nagata-final-descended-model], $S_{\lambda_Y}$ is Noetherian and $g$ is separated and of finite presentation. These are properties of the selected model itself; no replacement model or new compactification is chosen.

source.place: First sentence: Noetherian base and separated finitely presented descended morphism

proof.text: Finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] includes quasi-compactness. On affine charts a finitely presented algebra has the form $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$; the images of the finitely many $t_i$ generate it as an $A$-algebra, irrespective of the relations. Thus $g$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, hence of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This is the elementary implication of Stacks Tag 01TW (morphisms, lemma-finite-presentation-finite-type).

source.place: First sentence, the implication finite presentation hence finite type; Stacks Tag 01TW

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-noetherian] to $X=Y_{\lambda_Y}$, base $S_{\lambda_Y}$, and morphism $g$. Step 1 supplies the Noetherian base and separatedness, and step 2 supplies finite type. Its assertion about the recursively constructed factorization gives that $\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(Y_{\lambda_Y}/S_{\lambda_Y})$ is a compactification of $g$. We use this assertion about that construction, rather than merely its consequent that $g$ is compactifiable.

source.place: Second sentence: apply thm-nagata-noetherian to the explicitly selected recursive construction

proof.text: By [def-nagata-final-noetherian-compactification], $C_{Y,\lambda_Y}$ is precisely $\mathsf C_{\mathrm{Noeth}}(Y_{\lambda_Y}/S_{\lambda_Y})$. Substituting this defining equality in step 3 proves the assertion for the selected $C_{Y,\lambda_Y}$. In the terminology of [def-nagata-compactification], its factorization has a quasi-compact open immersion $j$, a proper map $p$, and $j;p=g$, as required.

source.place: Second sentence, identification of the explicitly selected construction with the object in the statement

proof_origin.place: Whole proof; elementary affine-algebra expansion of the first sentence using Stacks Tag 01TW
